finding.claim: The /mirror route's host check uses a suffix match (endswith 'example.com'), so an attacker-registered domain such as evilexample.com passes validation and the server issues a GET to an attacker-chosen host, including internal addresses via attacker-controlled DNS. Only the length of the response body is returned, so this is blind SSRF with a length oracle (MEDIUM).
finding.sink: httpx AsyncClient GET of the full user-supplied URL (mirror.py:16)

trace.note: url: str taken from the HTTP query string (attacker-controlled)
host = urlparse(url).hostname; correct accessor, but no exact-membership check follows
host.endswith('example.com') is a suffix check; evilexample.com passes; raises 400 only on mismatch
c.get(url) dispatches the request to the original unparsed URL with no scheme or IP-range restriction

finding.guards_checked: Suffix check at mirror.py:13 is insufficient (bypassable by any attacker-registrable domain ending in example.com). No scheme restriction. No RFC-1918, loopback, link-local or metadata IP block. No DNS-rebinding defence. Redirects: httpx AsyncClient does not follow redirects by default (httpx >= 0.20), so no redirect pivot found; re-verify if version or client options change. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is unused and has no effect. Hardcoded /ping (mirror.py:23) is not user-influenced and is excluded.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the suffix test at mirror.py:13 (`host.endswith("example.com")`), which does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused. No scheme, IP-range, or exact-membership check exists before the sink at mirror.py:16.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter (mirror.py:11) is unauthenticated input; urlparse(url).hostname (mirror.py:12) passes any host ending in "example.com" (e.g. evilexample.com) through the suffix-only check at mirror.py:13, and c.get(url) at mirror.py:16 then fetches the full attacker-chosen URL. httpx.AsyncClient does not follow redirects by default, so the redirect-pivot claim is not a refutation.
